verdict.line: You lose if you walk into his Cannon-stance poke before level 3; you win once Infernal Chains (W) and World Ender (R) let you force the fight on your terms.

brief.thesis: Jayce's ranged Cannon-stance poke only wins the lane if he keeps you at range; Aatrox's W (Infernal Chains) creates an impact zone that drags Jayce to its center and hits him a second time if he doesn't immediately move out, which punishes exactly the standing-and-kiting pattern Jayce relies on. That threat, plus a much stronger level-6 all-in, is why Aatrox holds the measured edge — 51.9% over 4,631 games, with both lane and solo-kill advantage — despite being outranged early.

theirWindow.when: Jayce is in Cannon stance at range
theirWindow.what: Don't walk forward to trade. In Cannon stance his Q (Shock Blast) hits all enemies in its path and his W (Hyper Charge) gives him max attack speed for several autos — stepping into either just feeds him free damage. Last-hit from behind minions and wait him out.

yourWindow.when: after your W lands or he transforms stances
yourWindow.what: The moment Infernal Chains connects, chain your E (Umbral Dash) in to close the gap and start swinging Q — each hit heals you via E's passive and progresses Deathbringer Stance. Stance swaps also cost him a global cooldown on R, so punish the swap itself before he's reset.

start.why: Taken in 72.9% of games at 52.4% win rate — the flat damage reduction on being hit by abilities directly offsets Shock Blast and Hyper Charge auto chip while you wait for level 3.

boots.why: 88.2% pick rate at 51.6% win rate. The attack damage reduction specifically dulls his Hyper Charge auto-attack bursts in Cannon stance.

core.why: Shield on double-hit punishes the exact moment he transforms stance to disengage, and softens his poke if he lands one first.
On-hit healing and a guaranteed critical on your first strike reward landing W into a Q string rather than trading autos at range.
Converts the burst damage from Shock Blast and Thundering Blow into damage-over-time you can heal through mid-fight, completing the 58.6% win-rate path over 355 games.

situational.when: you're ahead and want faster Q and E cooldowns to chain fights instead of resetting
he's consistently escaping in Cannon stance before your E (Umbral Dash) closes the gap
the game runs long and you need armor shred to keep killing him through Mercury Cannon's bonus resistances
he's building toward hard CC or his ignite/exhaust-less summoners let him kite you down repeatedly

runes.keystoneWhy: Rewards exactly the extended-trade pattern your kit wants — stack it closing distance with E, then cash it in during the W-pull all-in for AD and healing that outlasts his poke.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite is the 68.5%-pick, 52.9%-win-rate standard — it converts your solo-kill advantage into actual kills once W lands and R is up. Flash + Teleport (26.1% pick, 50.2% win rate) is the fallback if you're prioritizing wave management and scaling over forcing early fights.

playing.title: Hold position in Cannon stance
playing.detail: Don't approach while he's ranged — his Q hits everything in its path and his attack-speed burst from W punishes any trade. Let him come to melee range or back off.

playing.title: Hook with Infernal Chains on cooldown
playing.detail: Throw W at any opportunity once it's up at level 3 — if he doesn't immediately leave the impact zone he gets dragged in and hit twice, which is how you convert a ranged matchup into a melee one.

playing.title: Punish the stance swap
playing.detail: Every time he transforms via R he's committing to a new kit on a shared cooldown — dash in with E the instant he swaps, since he can't re-transform for several seconds.

playing.title: All-in the moment R is up
playing.detail: World Ender gives bonus AD, increased healing, and Move Speed at level 6 — this is your first guaranteed kill window if you can land W beforehand.

playing.title: Track your own Deathbringer Stance
playing.detail: Watch your passive icon before committing to extended trades — a free empowered auto with bonus magic damage and healing changes whether a fight is worth starting.

playing.title: Don't greed CS through his poke
playing.detail: Jayce's tip here is real: eating repeated Cannon-stance pokes to last-hit is how this lane flips. Give up marginal farm rather than take free damage.

playing.title: Close out with your item spike
playing.detail: Once Eclipse and Sundered Sky are both up, his poke damage stops mattering — start forcing fights on sight rather than waiting for cooldowns.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner spells, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG — the mechanical reasoning, timing windows, and trade patterns are my own analysis layered on top of that data, not measured values themselves.

stats.opponentTip: Do not get damaged by Jayce’s ranged (Q)-(E) pokes. After reaching level 3, use your skills whenever they come off cooldown to fight him.
